source_text: Ἰουδαῖοι δὲ πάντες καὶ νῦν διδάσκουσι τὸν ἀνωνόμαστον θεὸν λελαληκέναι τῷ Μωυσεῖ. Ὁθεν τὸ προφητικὸν πνεῦμα διὰ Ἡσαΐου τοῦ προμεμηνυμένου προφήτου ἐλέγχον αὐτούς, ὡς προεγράψαμεν, εἶπεν· „Ἔγνω βοῦς τὸν κτησάμενον καὶ ὄνος τὴν φάτνην τοῦ κυρίου αὐτοῦ, Ἰσραὴλ δέ με οὐκ ἔγνω καὶ ὁ λαός με οὐ συνῆκε“. Καὶ Ἰησοῦς δὲ ὁ Χριστός, ότι οὐκ ἔγνωσαν Ἰουδαῖοι, τί πατὴρ καὶ τί υἱός, ὁμοίως ἐλέγχων αὐτοὺς καὶ αὐτὸς εἶπεν· „Οὐδεὶς ἔγνω τὸν πατέρα εἰ μὴ ὁ υἱός, οὐδὲ τὸν υἱὸν εἰ μὴ ὁ πατὴρ καὶ οἷς ἂν ἀποκαλύψῃ ὁ υἱός“. Ὁ λόγος δὲ τοῦ θεοῦ ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς αὐτοῦ, ὡς προέφημεν. Καὶ ἄγγελος δὲ καλεῖται καὶ ἀπόστολος· αὐτὸς γὰρ ἀπαγγέλλει, ὅσα δεῖ γνωσθῆναι, καὶ ἀποστέλλεται μηνύσων, ὅσα ἀγγέλλεται, ὡς καὶ αὐτὸς ἱ κύριος ἡμῶν εἶπεν· „Ὁ ἐμοῦ ἀκούων ἀκούει τοῦ ἀποστείλαντός με“. Καὶ ἐκ τῶν τοῦ Μωϋσέως δὲ συγγραμμάτων φανερὸν τοῦτο γενήσεται. Λέλεκται δὲ ἐν αὐτοῖς οὕτως· „Καὶ ἐλάλησε Μωϋσεῖ ἄγγελος θεοῦ ἐν φλογὶ πυρὸς ἐκ τῆς βάτου καὶ εἶπεν· Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ὤν, θεὸς Ἀβραάμ, θεὸς Ἰσαάκ, θεὸς Ἰακώβ, ὁ θεὸς τῶν πατέρων σου. Κάτελθε εἰς Αἰγυπτον καὶ ἐξάγαγε τὸν λαόν μου“. Τὰ δ᾿ ἑπόμενα ἐξ ἐκείνων βουλόμενοι μαθεῖν δύνασθε· οὐ γὰρ δυνατὸν ἐν τούτοις ἀναγράψαι πάντα. Ἀλλ᾿ εἰς ἀπόδειξιν γεγόνασιν οἵδε οἱ λόγοι, ότι υἱὸς θεοῦ καὶ ἀπόστολος ᾿Ιησοῦς ὁ Χριστός ἐστι, πρότερον λόγος ὤν, καὶ ἐν ἰδέᾳ πυρὶ ς ποτὲ φανείς, ποτὲ δὲ καὶ ἐν εἰκόνι ἀσωμάτῳ· νῦν δὲ διὰ θελήματος θεοῦ ὑπὲρ τοῦ ἀνθρωπείου γένους ἄνθρωπος γενόμενος ὑπέμεινε καὶ παθεῖν, ὅσα αὐτὸν ἐνήργησαν οἱ δαίμονες διατεθῆναι ὑπὸ τῶν ἀνοήτων Ἰουδαίων. Οἵτινες ἔχοντες ῥητῶς εἰρημένον ἐν τοῖς Μωϋσέως συντάγμασι· „Καὶ ἐλάλησεν ἄγγελος τοῦ θεοῦ τῷ Μωϋσεῖ ἐν πυρὶ φλογὸς ἐν βάτῳ καὶ εἶπεν· Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ὤν, ἱ θεὸς Ἀβραὰμ καὶ ὁ θεὸς Ἰσαὰκ καὶ ὁ θεὸς Ἰακώβ“, τὸν τῶν όλων πατέρα καὶ δημιουργὸν τὸν ταῦτα εἰπόντα λέγουσιν εἶναι. Ὅθεν καὶ τὸ προφητικὸν πνεῦμα ἐλέγχον αὐτοὺς εἶπεν· „Ἰσραὴλ δέ με οὐκ ἔγνω, καὶ ὁ λαός με οὐ συνῆκε“. Καὶ πάλιν ὁ Ἰησοῦς, ὡς ἐδηλώσαμεν, παρ᾿ αὐτοῖς ἂν εἶπεν· „Οὐδεὶς ἔγνω τὸν πατέρα εἰ μἰ ὁ υἱός, οὐδὲ τὸν υἱὸν εἰ μὴ ὁ πατὴρ καὶ οἷς ἂν ἱ υἱὸς ἀποκαλύψῃ“. Ἰουδαῖοι οὖν ἡγησάμενοι ἀεὶ τὸν πατέρα τᾶν ὅλων λελαληκέναι τῷ Μωϋσεῖ, τοῦ λαλήσαντος αὐτῷ ὄντος υἱοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ, ὃς καὶ ἄγγελος καὶ ἀπόστολος κέκληται, δικαίως ἐλέγχονται καὶ διὰ τοῦ προφητικοῦ πνεύματος καὶ δι᾿ αὐτοῦ τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὡς οὔτε τὸν πατέρα οὔτε τὸν υἱὸν ἔγνωσαν. Οἱ γὰρ τὸν υἱὸν πατέρα φάσκοντες εἶναι ἐλέγχονται μήτε τὸν πατέρα ἐπιστάμενοι, μηθ᾿ ότι ἐστὶν υἱὸς τῷ πατρὶ τῶν ὅλων γινώσκοντες· ὃς λόγος καὶ πρωτότοκος ὢν τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ θεὶς ὑπάρχει. Καὶ πρότερον διὰ τῆς τοῦ πυρὸς μορφῆς καὶ εἰκόνος ἀσωμάτου τῷ Μωϋσεῖ καὶ τοῖς ἑτέροις προφήταις ἐφάνη· νῦν δ᾿ ἐν χρόνοις τῆς ὑμετέρας ἀρχῆς, ὡς προείπομεν, διὰ παρθένου ἄνθρωπος γενόμενος κατὰ τὴν τοῦ πατρὸς βουλὴν ὑπὲρ σωτηρίας τῶν πιστευόντων αὐτῷ καὶ ἐξουθενηθῆναι καὶ παθεῖν ὑπέμενεν, ἵνα ἀποθανὼν καὶ ἀναστὰς νικήσῃ τὸν θάνατον. Τὶ δὲ εἰρημένον ἐκ βάτου τῷ Μωϋσεῖ· „Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ὤν, ὁ θεὸς Ἀβραὰμ καὶ ὁ θεὸς Ἰσαὰκ καὶ ὁ θεὸς Ἰακὼβ καὶ ὁ θεὸς τῶν πατέρων σου“, σημαντικὸν τοῦ καὶ ἀποθανόντας ἐκείνους μένειν καὶ εἶναι αὐτοῦ τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἀνθρώπους· καὶ γὰρ πρῶτοι τῶν πάντων ἀνθρώπων ἐκεῖνοι περὶ θεοῦ ζήτησιν ἠσχολήθησαν, Ἀβραὰμ μὲν πατὴρ ὢν τοῦ Ἰσαάκ, Ἰσαὰκ δὲ τοῦ Ἰακώβ, ὡς καὶ Μωϋσῆς ἀνέγραψε.
pass_a_gloss: Jews all and now teach the unnamed God spoke to Moses. From which the prophetic Spirit through Isaiah the aforementioned prophet, reproving them, as we wrote before, said: 'A bull knows the one who acquired it and a donkey the manger of its Lord, but Israel does not know me and my people do not understand me.' And Jesus the Christ, because Jews do not know what father and what son are, similarly reproving them, also said: 'No one knows the Father except the Son, nor the Son except the Father and those to whom the Son reveals.' But the Word of God is His Son, as we said before. And He is called an angel and an apostle; for He announces what must be known and is sent to declare what He announces, just as the Lord Himself said: 'The one who hears me hears the one who sent me.' And from Moses' writings this will become clear. For it is written in them thus: 'And an angel of God spoke to Moses in a flame of fire from the bush and said: I am the one who is, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, the God of Jacob, the God of your fathers. Go down to Egypt and lead out my people.' The things that follow from those writings, if you want to learn, you are able; for it is not possible to write all things here. But these words have come to be for proof that Jesus the Christ is the Son of God and an apostle, having been the Word before, and having appeared at one time in the appearance of fire and at another time in an incorporeal image; now, however, having become a man through the will of God on behalf of the human race, He endured and suffered what the demons, having been handed over by the senseless Jews, worked against Him. Who, having it said plainly in Moses' writings: 'And an angel of God spoke to Moses in a flame of fire in the bush and said: I am the one who is, the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob', say that the Father of all, the one who said these things, is the one they mean. From which also the prophetic Spirit, reproving them, said: 'But Israel does not know me and my people do not understand me.' And again Jesus, as we showed, would say to them: 'No one knows the Father except the Son, nor the Son except the Father and those to whom the Son reveals.' Therefore, Jews, having always thought that the Father of all spoke to Moses, whereas the one who spoke to him was the Son of God, who is also called an angel and an apostle, are justly reproved both through the prophetic Spirit and through Christ Himself, as not knowing either the Father or the Son. For those who say the Son is the Father are reproved for not knowing the Father, nor that He has a Son, the Father of all; who, being the Word and the firstborn of God, exists. And previously, through the form of fire and an incorporeal image, He appeared to Moses and the other prophets; now, however, in the times of your rule, as we said before, having become a man through a virgin according to the will of the Father for the salvation of those who believe in Him, He endured to be despised and to suffer, so that having died and risen, He might conquer death. But what was said to Moses from the bush: 'I am the one who is, the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob and the God of your fathers', signifies that even though they died, they remain and are people of Christ; for they were the first of all people to be concerned with the search for God, Abraham being the father of Isaac, and Isaac of Jacob, just as Moses wrote.

pass_b_english: Even today, all Jews teach that the unnamed God spoke directly to Moses. The prophetic Spirit, speaking through the prophet Isaiah, rebukes them for this, just as we noted earlier: 'An ox knows its owner, and a donkey its master's manger, but Israel does not know me; my people do not understand' (Isaiah 1:3). Jesus the Christ likewise rebuked them, because they do not grasp what 'Father' and 'Son' mean. He said: 'No one knows the Father except the Son, and no one knows the Son except the Father, and those to whom the Son chooses to reveal him' (Matthew 11:27). The Word of God is that Son, as we have already said. He is also called Angel and Apostle, for he announces what must be known and is sent to proclaim what he announces—exactly as our Lord himself declared: 'Whoever hears me hears the one who sent me.' This point will become clear from the writings of Moses. Scripture records: 'An angel of God spoke to Moses in a flame of fire from the bush and said: I am the one who is, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, the God of Jacob, the God of your fathers. Go down to Egypt and lead out my people' (Exodus 3:2-4:17). You can learn the details that follow from those passages yourselves; it is not possible to write everything here. These words exist to prove that Jesus the Christ is the Son of God and an Apostle. He was the Word before all things, and he once appeared in the form of fire and again in an incorporeal image. Now, however, by God's will and for the sake of humanity, he became a man. He endured suffering at the hands of demons who incited senseless Jews against him—Jews who, despite having the plain statement in Moses: 'An angel of God spoke to Moses in a flame of fire in the bush and said: I am the one who is, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, the God of Jacob,' insist that the one who spoke was the Father of all, the Creator. Therefore the prophetic Spirit rebukes them again: 'Israel does not know me; my people do not understand.' Jesus also said to them, as we have shown: 'No one knows the Father except the Son, nor the Son except the Father, and those to whom the Son reveals him.' Jews have always assumed that the Father of all spoke to Moses, yet the one who spoke was the Son of God, who is also called Angel and Apostle. They are justly rebuked both by the prophetic Spirit and by Christ himself, because they know neither the Father nor the Son. Those who claim the Son is the Father are rebuked for knowing neither the Father nor the fact that the Father of all has a Son—the Word, the firstborn of God, who exists as God. Earlier he appeared to Moses and the other prophets through the form of fire and an incorporeal image. Now, in the era of your rule, as we said before, he became a man through a virgin by the Father's will, for the salvation of those who believe in him. He endured contempt and suffering so that by dying and rising he might conquer death. The words spoken to Moses from the bush—'I am the one who is, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, the God of Jacob, the God of your fathers'—signify that those patriarchs, though they died, remain alive and belong to Christ. They were the first of all humanity to seek God: Abraham fathered Isaac, Isaac fathered Jacob, just as Moses recorded.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the theological nuances of the Greek text, specifically the distinction between the 'unnamed God' and the Son acting as 'angel and apostle'. Pass A preserves the clause structure and the specific nuances of the Greek (e.g., 'incorporeal image' for εἰκόνι ἀσωμάτῳ). Pass B provides appropriate scripture citations (Isaiah 1:3, Matthew 11:27, Exodus 3:2-4:17) that correspond to the quoted/alluded text. The title 'Jews' Lack of Understanding' correctly identifies the central theme of the chapter.
